question: Let l,r be arbitrary natural numbers, possibly zero. Let A be a real l by (2r) matrix whose columns are indexed by (bit,new bond) in Fin 2 × Fin r, and assume AAᵀ=I_l. Define M(v)=∑_a v_a² for real row vectors. Proposition P: for every real row boundary v in R^l, M(vA)=M(v). Decide P and explain the input/output orientation and the role of normalization.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

question: Let l,r,A and M be as follows: A is a real matrix with old-bond rows Fin l and output columns Fin 2 × Fin r, AAᵀ=I_l, and M(w)=∑_i w_i². Proposition P: every real row boundary v satisfies M(vA)=1. No further assumption on v is supplied. Decide P, and if it fails give exact dimensions, entries and a boundary, then state the minimum extra premise or corrected conclusion.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

question: Let A be a real l × (2r) core, A_{a,(b,j)}, where a is the old bond, b∈Fin 2 the emitted bit and j∈Fin r the new bond. Assume AAᵀ=I_l. Form V with output rows ordered (new bond,bit) by V_{(j,b),a}=A_{a,(b,j)} as a complex number. Proposition P: V†V=I_l for arbitrary natural l,r. Decide P; explain exactly which register is permuted and whether a new normalization assumption is needed.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

question: There is one old-bond basis vector, one two-level physical bit and one two-level new bond. Let A be a real 1 × 4 row, indexed by (bit,new bond), with AAᵀ=[1]. Define U_{(b,j),0}=A_{0,(b,j)} as complex entries, and define V_{(j,b),0}=A_{0,(b,j)}. Both ordered output sets happen to be Fin 2 × Fin 2. Proposition P: V=U as matrices with the same literal pair labels, for every such A. Decide P, including an exact witness if needed and the correct relationship between entries.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

question: For arbitrary natural l,r let A be a real l × (2r) matrix with AAᵀ=I_l. Let U have output rows (bit,new bond)∈Fin 2 × Fin r and input columns a∈Fin l, with U_{out,a}=A_{a,out} embedded in C. Proposition P: UU†=I_(Fin 2 × Fin r). Decide P; give an exact finite witness if it fails and explain the dimension and physical-register issue.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

question: Let l,r be arbitrary natural numbers and A a real core indexed by old bond a and output (bit,new bond), with AAᵀ=I_l. Define U_{out,a}=A_{a,out} in C and define Q=UU†, a square matrix on the output space. Proposition P: Q²=Q. Decide P and explain whether this condition asserts Q=I or unitary state preparation on the full output register.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

question: Let f be any real amplitude table on n+1 binary wires, with no positivity or normalization assumption. For an n-bit prefix b define m(f)(b)=sqrt(f(b,0)²+f(b,1)²), where (b,v) means appending last bit v. For any table g define N(g)=∑_w g(w)². Proposition P: N(m(f))=N(f) for all natural n and all such f. Decide P and explain the precise normalization invariant it supplies to a recursive loader.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

question: On one binary wire identify a real table f with the pair (f(0),f(1)). Its zero-wire marginal m(f) is the one-entry table with value sqrt(f(0)²+f(1)²). Addition of tables is entrywise. Proposition P: for every real one-wire f,g, m(f+g)=m(f)+m(g). Decide P; explain what your result says about treating the norm-preserving marginal pass as a linear circuit isometry.
conventions: Equalities are exact. Fin n denotes the finite index set {0,...,n-1}; it is empty when n=0.

The controlled map is F_p(c,(s,x))=(c,(s,p_s(x))). The SELECT matrix is U_p(r,k)=1 if r=F_p(k), and 0 otherwise. Thus coefficient c and selector s are preserved, and no ancilla is added. All statements are exact equalities of matrices over ℂ; finite sets may be empty unless a concrete set is specified. Put D=X×(C×S), and let J(c,(s,x))=(x,(c,s)). Define U'_p(r,k)=U_p(J⁻¹(r),J⁻¹(k)). Decide whether the stated proposition is valid under exactly the supplied assumptions. Give a mathematical reason. question: Proposition P: for every natural number k and all real-coefficient polynomials p and q, if both have degree at most 2k+1, and all their ordinary derivatives of orders 0 through k agree at -1 and agree at 0, then p=q. Is P valid under the assumptions and conventions below?
assumptions: k is an arbitrary natural number, including zero; p and q are arbitrary real-coefficient polynomials, including the zero polynomial.
For every natural j with 0≤j≤k, the j-th ordinary derivatives of p and q agree at -1 and also agree at 0.
Both p and q have degree at most 2k+1 under the stated zero-polynomial convention.
conventions: Real polynomials and ordinary derivatives; the zero polynomial is allowed and satisfies the nonnegative degree bounds.
